correctness.rationale: The cyclic-Minkowski inequality yields the sharp universal ratio and fixes all edge norms in equality. The trace-duality normer lemma is derived from polar decompositions: a contraction that norms A and -B and a second that norms A and B force orthogonality of their right supports. Splitting the two opposite k-edge arcs gives positive B_i,C_i with identical sums and pairwise cross-orthogonality off diagonal. Positive diagonal traces yield a k-by-k full-rank pairing, hence d>=k. Diagonal matrix units construct an isometric embedding for d>=k. Finite-dimensional compactness makes the strict below-threshold gap genuine. Checker passed 5018 numerical assertions; these test only finite examples.

value.rationale: The matrix size is a natural finite-dimensional complexity invariant for realizing a geodesic metric inside the noncommutative trace norm. The exact threshold d=k holds for arbitrary nonlinear embeddings and nonnormal matrices. This is an entire infinite family of optimal finite cutoffs, and also classifies when the one-dimensional metric-cotype bound is attained; the polar-support obstruction has structural content beyond numerical reproducibility or a standard scalar estimate.
